description: wg-relay, a UDP relay for WireGuard peers behind NAT: traffic, drops and abuse signals, sessions, configured peers, forwarding threads and the process.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: The running build, from wg_relay_build_info.

panels.title: Started
panels.description: When the relay process started; a recent time means a restart, which zeroes every counter and session.

panels.title: Last reload
panels.description: Whether the last SIGHUP reload succeeded; failed means the previous config is still running.

panels.title: Configured peers
panels.description: Peers listed in the config.

panels.title: Registered peers
panels.description: Configured peers with a live registration; compare with configured peers.

panels.title: Unregistered peers
panels.description: Configured peers without a live registration: they cannot be reached through the relay. Should be 0.

panels.title: Forwarded
panels.description: Datagrams forwarded per second.

panels.title: Forwarded throughput
panels.description: UDP payload forwarded, in bits per second.

panels.title: Drop ratio
panels.description: Share of received datagrams dropped for any reason; a small steady share is normal (sessions that just expired or roamed), a jump means junk or a flood.

panels.title: Established sessions
panels.description: Established session entries (two per forwarded handshake, one per direction), including expired ones not yet collected.

panels.title: Pending sessions
panels.description: Forwarded initiations awaiting their response; a climb with few established sessions is an initiation flood.

panels.title: Workers
panels.description: Forwarding threads, each with its own socket.

panels.title: Datagrams
panels.description: Every received datagram is forwarded, delivered to a registration tunnel or dropped, so received is the sum of the other three.

panels.title: Bytes
panels.description: UDP payload bytes by outcome; forwarded bytes are the relay's useful work.

panels.title: Messages received by type
panels.description: Received datagrams that parsed as WireGuard messages; transport data should dominate, a rise in handshake initiations alone is handshake pressure.

panels.title: Messages forwarded by type
panels.description: Messages passed on unchanged; compare with the received panel to see which types are being dropped.

panels.title: Decided by plane
panels.description: Share of datagrams decided by the lock-free data plane versus the control plane under its lock; a rising control share means handshake or junk pressure.

panels.title: Registration tunnel traffic
panels.description: Datagrams the relay's registration tunnels took and sent; cookie replies are sent only when a tunnel is under load.

panels.title: Drops by reason
panels.description: Every dropped datagram, stacked by reason; a flood shows as one reason growing (rate_limited, no_mac1_match, unknown_index or a budget), a full table as too_many_sessions, too_many_pending or peer_quota.

panels.title: Top drop reasons
panels.description: Drops per reason over the selected time range, largest first, with the current rate.

panels.title: Half-open handshakes
panels.description: Pending sessions that expired unanswered against initiations forwarded; half-open close to forwarded means spoofed or junk initiations to a configured peer.

panels.title: Pending evictions
panels.description: Pending sessions pushed out by a newer initiation to the same configured peer; a steady rise is a flood aimed at one peer.

panels.title: Unknown-index drops
panels.description: Datagrams for an index with no live session; some always come from sessions that just expired or roamed, a level well above usual is junk data.

panels.title: Rate limited
panels.description: Initiations dropped because their source (IPv4 address or IPv6 /64) exceeded the per-source handshake rate, against all initiations received.

panels.title: Rate-limit buckets used
panels.description: Share of per-source rate-limit buckets any source has used since startup; they are never freed, so a fast climb means a flood from many sources and more sources sharing buckets.

panels.title: Handshake budgets remaining
panels.description: Mac1 checks each CPU budget would allow at scrape time; at or below 0 it drops initiations, including legitimate ones (the budget drop reasons confirm it between scrapes).

panels.title: Mac1 work
panels.description: Mac1 keys hashed and peer scans per second against the forwarding budget (dashed), which sits far above normal traffic; checks climbing toward it mean forwarded initiations are about to be dropped.

panels.title: Tunnel errors by kind
panels.description: Datagrams a registration tunnel refused; authentication or replay errors are someone probing the relay's own key, under_load is its handshake limit.

panels.title: Registration initiations
panels.description: Initiations to the relay itself that passed the rate limit: accepted by a registration tunnel, or rejected (budget, unknown key, failed authentication).

panels.title: Session table
panels.description: All session entries against the table's cap; refusals (too_many_sessions) start at 100%.

panels.title: Pending table
panels.description: Pending entries against their cap; refusals (too_many_pending) start at 100%.

panels.title: Sessions by state
panels.description: Session entries, stacked, so the top is the whole table; counts include expired entries until the next garbage collection.

panels.title: Table fullness
panels.description: Both tables against their caps over time; the dashed line at 80% is where to start worrying.

panels.title: Expirations by state
panels.description: Sessions removed at the end of their fixed lifetime; established ones expire on schedule, pending ones are half-open handshakes.

panels.title: Roams and revocations
panels.description: Session entries rewritten because their configured peer moved, and entries removed by a reload that removed their peer.

panels.title: Garbage collection
panels.description: Garbage collection passes, which remove expired sessions and registrations; a flat line at zero means collection stopped.

panels.title: Configured peers
panels.description: One row per configured peer: unregistered peers cannot be reached; a pending count near its per-peer cap or many dropped initiations means a flood against that peer.

panels.title: Initiations forwarded by peer
panels.description: Initiations whose mac1 named the peer and were forwarded to it; a spike against one peer singles out the target of a flood.

panels.title: Initiations dropped by peer
panels.description: Initiations for the peer dropped after the scan: not registered, at its quota, a loop, an index in use or a full table.

panels.title: Time since last authenticated
panels.description: Climbs between authenticated datagrams on the peer's registration tunnel and drops back on each; a line that keeps climbing means the peer has gone quiet and its registration will time out.

panels.title: Pending sessions by peer
panels.description: Initiations aimed at each peer awaiting its answer, against the per-peer cap beyond which a new one evicts the oldest.

panels.title: Established sessions by peer
panels.description: Established session entries routed to each peer, two per connected client handshake.

panels.title: Registrations
panels.description: New registrations, registered peers moving to a new endpoint, and registrations that timed out; expirations without new ones mean peers are dropping off.

panels.title: Datagrams per worker
panels.description: Datagrams each thread's data plane decided; the kernel spreads flows by address pair, so a few heavy flows can load one thread more than the others.

panels.title: Forwarded per worker
panels.description: Datagrams each thread's data plane forwarded.

panels.title: Share per worker

targets.expr: sum by (worker) (increase(wg_relay_worker_datagrams_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])) / ignoring (worker) group_left sum(increase(wg_relay_worker_datagrams_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))

panels.description: Each thread's share of the data plane's datagrams over the selected range; equal bars mean an even spread.

panels.title: Bytes per worker
panels.description: UDP payload bytes each thread's data plane decided.

panels.title: Forwarded bytes per worker
panels.description: UDP payload bytes each thread's data plane forwarded.

panels.title: Socket errors per worker
panels.description: Failed receives and sends on each thread's socket; a remote host can cause send errors, a burst on one thread points at one flow.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU time per second, user and system; 100% is one full core.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident and virtual memory; resident grows with the session table and gives memory back when garbage collection finds it mostly empty.

panels.title: Open file descriptors
panels.description: Open file descriptors; the soft limit is in the legend and tooltip rather than plotted, since it dwarfs normal use (absent when unlimited).

panels.title: Socket errors
panels.description: Failed socket receives and sends over all threads; logged individually only at debug level, since a remote host can cause them.

panels.title: Config reloads
panels.description: Reloads since start by result, as a step count; a step in failure is a SIGHUP whose config was rejected while the old one kept running.

panels.title: Config applied
panels.description: When the running config was applied, at startup or by the last successful reload.

title: wg-relay
